title: Final: platforms
sub: Server, window and game: one mechanism
cards/0/task: Find the environment where .Result doesn't hang.
cards/1/task: A Unity script moves the transform after await. Make it work without freezing frames.
cards/2/q: What do WPF and Unity have in common for async?
cards/2/options/0: Both install a SynchronizationContext on the main thread whose Post puts the continuation into that thread's queue
cards/2/options/1: Both run every continuation on a pool thread, and the main thread only renders
cards/2/options/2: Both forbid .Result at the compiler level
cards/2/explain: That's why .Result on the main thread hangs in both: the queue has to be drained by the very thread that's stuck on .Result.
cards/3/q: Where is ConfigureAwait(false) dangerous? Select all that apply.
cards/3/options/0: In a WPF handler that then changes a control
cards/3/options/1: In a Unity script that then touches the transform
cards/3/explain: After it the code runs on the pool: VerifyAccess in WPF and Unity's main-thread check will throw. In a library it helps, and in ASP.NET Core there's no context, so it changes nothing.
cards/4/explain: Without destroyCancellationToken the wait isn't cancelled if the object is destroyed, and the next line fails with MissingReferenceException.
cards/5/q: After a payment, an ASP.NET Core controller does _ = Task.Run(() => _mailer.SendReceiptAsync(order.Id)); _mailer is a scoped service with a DbContext inside. What's the right way?
cards/5/options/0: Put order.Id into a Channel queue, and a BackgroundService sends the email in its own scope
cards/5/options/1: Add ConfigureAwait(false) to SendReceiptAsync inside Task.Run
cards/5/options/2: Call SendReceiptAsync from an async void method so the error isn't lost
cards/5/explain: The scoped DbContext is disposed together with the request. Work after the response belongs in a BackgroundService that creates its own scope for each queue item.
cards/6/q: Put the continuation's path after await in WPF in order
cards/6/items/1: The operation completed on a pool thread
cards/6/items/2: Post calls Dispatcher.BeginInvoke: the continuation is queued to the UI thread
cards/6/items/3: The UI thread took it from the queue
cards/6/items/4: The code after await ran on the UI thread
cards/6/explain: If the UI thread is blocked on .Result at that moment, step 4 never comes: that's the deadlock.
cards/7/q: WPF: a Progress<int> is created in a button handler, and Report is called from Task.Run. Where does the Progress callback run?
cards/7/options/0: On the UI thread: Progress remembered the DispatcherSynchronizationContext and Posts to it
cards/7/options/1: On the pool thread that called Report
cards/7/options/2: Synchronously inside Report: the pool thread waits for the callback to run
cards/7/explain: Progress remembers the context in its constructor. Report only queues the callback and returns immediately.
cards/8/q: Unity 6. An object runs the Blink coroutine and an async Awaitable PatrolAsync with destroyCancellationToken at the same time. The object is deactivated: SetActive(false). What stops?
cards/8/explain: Unity stops the coroutine because it calls the coroutine's MoveNext itself. destroyCancellationToken is cancelled only when the object is destroyed.
cards/9/q: Match each platform to how await brings the continuation back
cards/9/pairs/2/1: A queue drained once per frame
cards/9/pairs/3/1: No context: the continuation runs on the pool
cards/10/q: Which rule saves the server, the window and the game alike?
cards/10/options/0: Async all the way: don't block async code with .Result and .Wait()
cards/10/explain: Blocking the main thread in WPF and Unity gives a deadlock, on a server it gives pool starvation. Task.Run and ConfigureAwait(false) are tools for specific places, not a general rule.
